answer: Require reputation that cannot be bought or transferred: an agent must forge a history of completed jobs, each signed by an independent client that verified the output, before joining high-value trades. A newcomer starts at zero, so the voyage to trusted status takes real time, compute, and successful deliveries, not a signup form. Only after a streak of verified jobs does the system issue a lotus credential, bound to that agent's key. An attacker creating thousands of identities must pay the full work cost for each one, making a sybil flood more expensive than any gain from an extra vote.
